questions.q: What is the seventh period (n = 7) known for?
questions.solution: The seventh period (n = 7) is similar to the sixth period with the successive filling up of the 7s, 5f, 6d and 7p orbitals and includes most of the man-made radioactive elements.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

questions.q: What are the p-Block Elements together with s-Block elements called?
options: Representative Elements or Main Group Elements
questions.solution: The p-Block Elements, together with the s-Block Elements, are called the Representative Elements or Main Group Elements.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

questions.q: What did Mendeleev do when some elements did not fit his scheme of classification based on atomic weights?
options: He revised the atomic weights of those elements.
He left gaps in the table and placed elements with similar properties together.
He excluded those elements from his periodic table.
questions.solution: When some elements did not fit his scheme of classification based on atomic weights, Mendeleev left gaps in the table and placed elements with similar properties together.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

questions.q: What term is used to describe the elements that come after uranium?
questions.solution: The elements that come after uranium are called Transuranium Elements.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

questions.q: How many blocks can the elements be classified into based on the type of atomic orbitals being filled with electrons?
questions.solution: We can classify the elements into four blocks viz., s-block, p-block, d-block, and f-block depending on the type of atomic orbitals that are being filled with electrons.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

questions.q: What does the period number in the Periodic Table correspond to?
questions.solution: The period number corresponds to the highest principal quantum number (n) of the elements in the period.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

questions.q: Why does boron (Z = 5) have a smaller first ionization enthalpy than beryllium (Z = 4)?
options: Boron has a greater nuclear charge.
questions.solution: Boron has a smaller first ionization enthalpy than beryllium because the 2p-electron of boron is more shielded from the nucleus by the inner core of electrons than the 2s electrons of beryllium.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

questions.q: Which group of elements is described as good conductors of heat and electricity?
questions.solution: Metals are good conductors of heat and electricity.

questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

questions.q: How many electrons does oxygen share with fluorine atoms in the OF<sub>2</sub> molecule?
questions.solution: Oxygen shares two electrons with fluorine atoms in the OF<sub>2</sub> molecule.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

questions.q: According to Newlands's Law of Octaves, what was the pattern of properties among elements?
options: Every third element had similar properties.
Every fourth element had similar properties.
Every seventh element had similar properties.
Every eighth element had similar properties.
questions.solution: According to Newlands's Law of Octaves, every eighth element had properties similar to the first element.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

questions.q: What is the atomic number equal to in a neutral atom?
options: Number of electrons in the outermost shell
questions.solution: The atomic number is equal to the nuclear charge (i.e., the number of protons) or the number of electrons in a neutral atom.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

questions.q: How many elements are there in the fourth period (n = 4) of the Periodic Table?
questions.solution: We have 18 elements in this fourth period.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

questions.q: What term is used to describe the elements in Group 18 of the Periodic Table?
questions.solution: Group 18 elements are referred to as noble gases.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

questions.q: What are elements with properties that are characteristic of both metals and non-metals called?
questions.solution: Elements with properties that are characteristic of both metals and non-metals are called Metalloids.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

questions.q: What type of oxide is formed by elements in the center of a period?
questions.solution: Oxides of elements in the center are amphoteric.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

questions.q: Which type of elements are "elements towards the middle of the table"?
questions.solution: Elements towards the middle of the table are typically transition metals.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

questions.q: What does the Periodic Law state?
options: The properties of elements are random.
The properties of elements depend on their atomic numbers.
The properties of elements are a periodic function of their atomic weights.
The properties of elements do not change.
questions.solution: The Periodic Law states that the properties of elements are a periodic function of their atomic weights.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

questions.q: What determines the placement of elements in the s-Block of the Periodic Table?
options: The number of protons in the nucleus
The number and distribution of electrons in the outermost orbitals
The number of neutrons in the nucleus
questions.solution: The elements of Group 1 (alkali metals) and Group 2 (alkaline earth metals) which have ns1 and ns2 outermost electronic configuration belong to the s-Block Elements.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

questions.q: What factor causes the increase in ionization enthalpy as you move across a period in the periodic table?
questions.solution: As you move across a period, increased electron-electron repulsion contributes to the increase in ionization enthalpy.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

questions.q: What is a common characteristic of Group 1 (alkali metals) and Group 2 (alkaline earth metals) in terms of ion formation?
options: They readily gain electrons to form anions.
They readily lose electrons to form cations.
They do not readily form ions.
They form both cations and anions equally.
questions.solution: They lose the outermost electron(s) readily to form 1+ ion (in the case of alkali metals) or 2+ ion (in the case of alkaline earth metals).
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

questions.q: What did the Periodic Law reveal about the naturally occurring elements?
options: They have analogies with synthetic elements.
They have analogies with other naturally occurring elements.
questions.solution: The Periodic Law revealed important analogies among the 94 naturally occurring elements.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

questions.q: Up to which element did Newlands's Law of Octaves seem to be true?
questions.solution: Newlands's Law of Octaves seemed to be true only for elements up to calcium.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

questions.q: How many Periods are there in the Periodic Table?
questions.solution: There are altogether seven Periods in the Periodic Table.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

questions.q: Which element can only form BF<sub>4</sub> in terms of covalency?
questions.solution: Boron can only form BF<sub>4</sub> in terms of covalency.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

questions.q: What term did Dobereiner use to describe the groups of three elements with similar properties?
questions.solution: Dobereiner used the term "Triads" to describe the groups of three elements with similar properties.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

questions.q: What is the trend in atomic radii change among transition metals (3d series) compared to representative elements?
options: The change is larger among transition metals.
The change is smaller among transition metals.
The change is the same for both.
questions.solution: The change in atomic radii is much smaller among transition metals (3d series) compared to representative elements.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

questions.q: Which type of oxides are formed by elements on the extreme left and extreme right of a period?
questions.solution: The element on the extreme left forms basic oxides, and the element on the extreme right forms acidic oxides.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

questions.q: Which element has the valence shell electronic configuration [Ne]3s1?
questions.solution: The valence shell electronic configuration for potassium (K) as "[Ar]4s1," which is equivalent to [Ne]3s23p64s1 in the given format.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

questions.q: Who was the first scientist to consider the idea of trends among properties of elements?
questions.solution: The German chemist, Johann Dobereiner, in the early 1800s, was the first to consider the idea of trends among properties of elements.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

questions.q: Why is helium positioned in the p-block of the Periodic Table?
options: Because it has a completely filled valence shell
Because it has a high atomic number
Because it belongs to the alkali metals
Because it has a half-filled valence shell
questions.solution: Strictly, helium belongs to the s-block but its positioning in the p-block along with other group 18 elements is justified because it has a completely filled valence shell (1s2) and as a result, exhibits properties characteristic of other noble gases.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

questions.q: What is the maximum covalency of the first member of each group?
questions.solution: The maximum covalency of the first member of each group is 4.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

questions.q: What is the common valence shell electronic configuration for Group 1 elements (alkali metals)?
questions.solution: The Group 1 elements (alkali metals) all have ns1 valence shell electronic configuration like Li have [He]2s1, Na have [Ne]3s1 and so on.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

questions.q: In a group of representative metals like alkali metals, what happens to reactivity as you move down the group?
questions.solution: Within a group of representative metals, such as alkali metals, reactivity increases as you move down the group.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

questions.q: How is the atomic size determined if it cannot be precisely measured for an individual atom?
options: By measuring the radius of a ball
By measuring the electron cloud boundary
By measuring the distance between combined atoms
questions.solution: The atomic size can be estimated by knowing the distance between atoms in the combined state.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

questions.q: Within a period, where do elements with lower chemical reactivity tend to be located?
options: At the beginning of the period
In the middle of the period
At the end of the period
They are evenly distributed throughout the period
questions.solution: Elements with lower chemical reactivity tend to be located towards the middle of a period.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

questions.q: What is the basis for the systematic nomenclature recommended by the IUPAC for new elements?
options: The atomic number of the element.
questions.solution: A systematic nomenclature be derived directly from the atomic number of the element using the numerical roots for 0 and numbers 1-9.The roots are put together in order of digits which make up the atomic number and “ium” is added at the end. Like for a element with atomic number 112, its name will be Ununbium.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

questions.q: How are successive Periods in the Periodic Table associated with principal energy levels?
options: They are not associated with energy levels.
Each period is associated with the same energy level.
Each period is associated with the filling of the next higher principal energy level.
Each period is associated with a random energy level.
questions.solution: Successive period in the Periodic Table is associated with the filling of the next higher principal energy level (n = 1, n = 2, etc.).
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

questions.q: What is the "Covalent Radius" used to estimate?
options: The size of an individual atom
The size of a metallic element
The metallic radius of an element
questions.solution: The "Covalent Radius" is used to estimate the size of an individual non-metallic atom.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

questions.q: What are the fundamental properties of an element?
options: Atomic and ionic radii, ionization enthalpy, electron gain enthalpy, and valence
Transition metals and main group elements
questions.solution: The fundamental properties are atomic and ionic radii, ionization enthalpy, electron gain enthalpy, and valence.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

questions.q: What term is frequently used for valence nowadays?
questions.solution: Nowadays the term oxidation state is frequently used for valence.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

questions.q: Why are elements of Group 1 (alkali metals) and Group 2 (alkaline earth metals) never found pure in nature?
options: Because they are extremely rare elements
Because they readily react with other elements and compounds
Because they have high ionization enthalpies
Because they are always found as noble gases
questions.solution: Because of high reactivity Group 1 and Group 2 elements are never found pure in nature.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

questions.q: How does the metallic character and reactivity of Group 1 and Group 2 elements change as you move down the group?
questions.solution: The metallic character and the reactivity increase as we go down the group.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

questions.q: Why are the 4f- and 5f-inner transition series of elements placed separately in the Periodic Table?
options: To create more space in the table.
To maintain the periodic table's structure.
To make the table look symmetrical.
To separate elements with similar properties.
questions.solution: The 4f- and 5f-inner transition series of elements are placed separately in the Periodic Table to maintain its structure and to preserve the principle of classification by keeping elements with similar properties in a single column.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

questions.q: Which elements are included in the second period of the periodic table?
questions.solution: The second period includes elements from lithium to fluorine.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

questions.q: What is the reason for the increased shielding as you move down a group in the periodic table?
options: The outermost electrons are closer to the nucleus.
The outermost electrons experience greater attraction to the nucleus.
The inner core of electrons is more filled.
The number of electrons in the outermost shell increases.
questions.solution: The increased shielding occurs when the orbitals in the inner shells are completely filled, which happens in the case of alkali metals with a noble gas electronic configuration.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

questions.q: Which elements are usually solids or gases at room temperature?
questions.solution: Non-metals are usually solids or gases at room temperature.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

questions.q: What is the "Metallic Radius" used to estimate?
options: The size of an individual atom
The size of a covalent molecule
The distance between metal cores in a metallic crystal
The covalent radius of a metal
questions.solution: The "Metallic Radius" is used to estimate the size of a metal and is taken as half the internuclear distance separating the metal cores in the metallic crystal.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

questions.q: In which family does hydrogen exhibit properties similar to when it gains an electron?
questions.solution: Hydrogen can also gain an electron to achieve a noble gas arrangement and hence it can behave similar to a group 17 (halogen family) elements.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

questions.q: Which group of elements is an example of increasing reactivity as you move down the group?
questions.solution: Alkali metals are given as an example of a group of elements where reactivity increases as you move down the group.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

questions.q: In which direction does the reactivity of non-metals within a group (e.g., halogens) change?
questions.solution: Within a group of non-metals (e.g., halogens), reactivity decreases down the group.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

questions.q: Which element is an exception because it is a liquid at room temperature?
questions.solution: Mercury is an exception because it is a liquid at room temperature.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

questions.q: Which elements in the s-Block of the Periodic Table have predominantly ionic compounds, with exceptions?
options: All s-Block elements have predominantly ionic compounds.
Only Group 1 elements have predominantly ionic compounds.
Only Group 2 elements have predominantly ionic compounds.
All s-Block elements have predominantly covalent compounds.
questions.solution: The compounds of the s-block elements, with the exception of those of lithium and beryllium, are predominantly ionic.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

questions.q: What did Mendeleev predict about the properties of gallium and germanium?
options: He predicted they would have no properties.
He predicted they would have completely different properties from other elements.
He predicted some of their general physical properties.
He predicted they would be radioactive.
questions.solution: Mendeleev predicted some of the general physical properties of gallium and germanium.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

questions.q: According to the recommendation of IUPAC, how are the groups in the Periodic Table numbered?
questions.solution: According to the recommendation of International Union of Pure and Applied Chemistry (IUPA

questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

questions.q: Which series of elements is characterized by the filling of f-orbitals?
questions.solution: The Actinoid series is characterized by the filling of f-orbitals.

questions.q: How many electrons are in the outermost orbitals of fluorine?
questions.solution: Fluorine has an outer electronic configuration of "2s22p5."

questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

questions.q: Which series of elements is known as the 4f-inner transition series?
questions.solution: The 4f-inner transition series as the lanthanoid series.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

questions.q: What type of elements become more metallic as one goes down a group on the Periodic Table?
questions.solution: Metals become more metallic as one goes down a group on the Periodic Table.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

questions.q: Why do noble gases have large positive electron gain enthalpies?
options: They have stable noble gas electronic configurations.
They have to enter the next higher principal quantum level.
questions.solution: Noble gases have large positive electron gain enthalpies because the added electron has to enter the next higher principal quantum level, leading to a very unstable electronic configuration.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

questions.q: What did Johann Dobereiner note about the physical and chemical properties of several groups of three elements?
questions.solution: Johann Dobereiner noted a similarity among the physical and chemical properties of several groups of three elements, which he referred to as Triads.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

questions.q: What are the horizontal rows in the Periodic Table called?
questions.solution: The horizontal rows in the Periodic Table are called Periods.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

questions.q: How is the metallic radius of copper determined?
options: By measuring the electron cloud radius
By measuring the bond distance in a copper molecule (Cu<sub>2</sub>)
By measuring the distance between two adjacent copper atoms in solid copper
By measuring the distance between two copper ions
questions.solution: The metallic radius of copper is determined by measuring the distance between two adjacent copper atoms in solid copper.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

questions.q: What do the chalcogens readily add to attain the stable noble gas configuration?
questions.solution: The chalcogens (Group 16) readily add electrons to attain the stable noble gas configuration.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

questions.q: What recommendation has the IUPAC made to avoid naming disputes for new elements?
options: The IUPAC recommends that new elements should be named after famous scientists.
The IUPAC recommends that new elements should not be named until their discovery is proven.
The IUPAC recommends that new elements should be named by the first laboratory to synthesize them.
The IUPAC recommends that new elements should be named after the laboratory where they were discovered.
questions.solution: To avoid problems, the IUPAC has made a recommendation that until a new element’s discovery is proved, and its name is officially recognised, a systematic nomenclature be derived directly from the atomic number of the element using the numerical roots for 0 and numbers 1-9.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

questions.q: Why do group 17 elements (the halogens) have very high negative electron gain enthalpies?
options: They have stable noble gas electronic configurations.
They have low effective nuclear charge.
questions.solution: Halogens have very high negative electron gain enthalpies because they can attain stable noble gas electronic configurations by picking up an electron.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

questions.q: Which elements are usually solids at room temperature?
questions.solution: Metals are usually solids at room temperature.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

questions.q: How many elements are there in the second period of the Periodic Table?
questions.solution: The first period contains 2 elements.The subsequent Periods consist of 8, 8, 18, 18, and 32 elements, respectively.

questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

questions.q: What were two examples of Eka-elements?
questions.solution: Two examples of Eka-elements mentioned in the paragraph are gallium and germanium.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

questions.q: How many valence orbitals are available for bonding in the first member of a group in the s- and p-blocks?
questions.solution: The first member of the group has only four valence orbitals (2s and 2p) available for bonding.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

questions.q: Which elements have the electronic configuration (n-1)d10ns2?
questions.solution: Zn, Cd, and Hg have the electronic configuration (n-1)d10ns2.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

questions.q: Which two groups of non-metals precede the noble gas family?
questions.solution: Preceding the noble gas family are two chemically important groups of non-metals, which are the chalcogens (Group 16) and the halogens (Group 17).
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

questions.q: How do ionization enthalpies of transition elements (3d series) compare to those of group 1 and 2 metals?
questions.solution: Transition elements (3d series) are less electropositive than group 1 and 2 metals, indicating that their ionization enthalpies are higher.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

questions.q: What can the other members of the groups do regarding their valence shell compared to the first member?
options: They have the same number of valence orbitals.
They can expand their valence shell to accommodate more than four pairs of electrons.
questions.solution: The other members of the groups can expand their valence shell to accommodate more than four pairs of electrons.

questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

questions.q: Which element is an example of the first member of p-block elements forming multiple bonds to itself?
questions.solution: The first member of p-block elements displays greater ability to form p<sub>π</sub> – p<sub>π</sub>  multiple bonds to itself e.g., C = C, C ≡ C, N = N, N ≡ Ν.

questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

questions.q: How does the penetration of electrons to the nucleus affect ionization enthalpy?
options: Penetration has no effect on ionization enthalpy.
It depends on the specific electron orbitals.
questions.solution: Greater penetration of electrons to the nucleus decreases ionization enthalpy, as seen in the case of boron and beryllium.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

questions.q: How are elements arranged within the vertical columns or groups in the Periodic Table?
questions.solution: The elements having similar outer electronic configurations in their atoms are arranged in vertical columns, referred to as groups or families.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

questions.q: Which elements are specifically studied for their anomalous properties?
questions.solution: The anomalous properties of the second period elements are being studied.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

questions.q: Which Periods are mentioned as having a theoretical maximum number of 32 elements?
questions.solution: Both the sixth and seventh Periods (lanthanoids and actinoids, respectively) would have a theoretical maximum of 32 elements based on quantum numbers.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

questions.q: What is the electron gain enthalpy of the halogens?
questions.solution: The halogens (Group 17) have highly negative electron gain enthalpies.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

questions.q: What is the trend of electronegativity across a period in the periodic table?
options: It increases from left to right.
It decreases from left to right.
It depends on the specific period.
questions.solution: Electronegativity generally increases across a period from left to right in the periodic table.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

questions.q: Who traditionally had the privilege of naming new elements, and how was the suggested name ratified?
options: Only the discoverer had the privilege, and the name was ratified by the IUPAC.
Only the IUPAC had the privilege, and the name was ratified by the discoverer.
Both the discoverer and the IUPAC had the privilege, and they jointly ratified the name.
Naming of new elements was done randomly without any privileges or ratification.
questions.solution: The naming of the new elements had been traditionally the privilege of the discoverer (or discoverers) and the suggested name was ratified by the IUPAC.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

questions.q: What happens to the atomic size as you move across a period in the periodic table?
questions.solution: The atomic size generally decreases across a period in the periodic table due to the increased attraction of electrons to the nucleus as the atomic number increases.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

questions.q: Why would a cation with a greater positive charge have a smaller radius?
options: Because of greater attraction of electrons to the nucleus
questions.solution: A cation with a greater positive charge will have a smaller radius because of the greater attraction of the electrons to the nucleus.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

questions.q: What did Mendeleev arrange in horizontal rows and vertical columns in his periodic table?
questions.solution: Mendeleev arranged elements in horizontal rows and vertical columns in his periodic table based on elements with similar properties.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

questions.q: What is the common state of matter for the Lanthanoids and Actinoids?
questions.solution: The Lanthanoids and Actinoids are primarily in the solid state of matter.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

questions.q: How does the nuclear charge affect the size of an ion?
options: Higher nuclear charge leads to a larger ion
Higher nuclear charge leads to a smaller ion
Nuclear charge has no effect on ion size
Higher nuclear charge makes the ion unstable
questions.solution: A cation with a greater positive charge (higher nuclear charge) will have a smaller radius.

questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

questions.q: What aspect of atomic structure and properties of the atom must be explored to answer the questions about periodicity?
options: Number of electrons and energy levels
questions.solution: To answer questions about the properties of elements and periodicity, the paragraph suggests that we must look into the theories of atomic structure and properties of the atom, specifically focusing on the number of electrons and energy levels.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

questions.q: How does the concept of shielding or screening affect the ionization enthalpy?
options: It has no effect on the ionization enthalpy.
It depends on the specific element.
questions.solution: The shielding or screening of the valence electron from the nucleus by the intervening core electrons decreases the effective nuclear charge experienced by a valence electron, making ionization easier.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

questions.q: What happens to the ionic radius of an anion when one or more electrons are added to it?
questions.solution: The addition of one or more electrons to an anion results in a larger ionic radius.

questions.q: How does the atomic radius change within a family or vertical column of the periodic table?
options: It decreases regularly with atomic number
It increases regularly with atomic number
It depends on the type of elements in the family
questions.solution: Within a family or vertical column of the periodic table, the atomic radius increases regularly with atomic number.

questions.q: How many exceptions to the classification of elements into blocks are there?
questions.solution: Helium belongs to the s-block but its positioning in the p-block along with other group 18 elements is justified because it has a completely filled valence shell (1s1) and as a result, exhibits properties characteristic of other noble gases. The other exception is hydrogen. It has only one s-electron and hence can be placed in group 1 (alkali metals). It can also gain an electron to achieve a noble gas arrangement and hence it can behave similar to a group 17 (halogen family) elements. Because it is a special case, we shall place hydrogen separately at the top of the Periodic Table.

questions.q: What is the term for oxides that behave as acidic with bases and as basic with acids?

Assertion (A) Electronic configuration of boron \((Z=5)\) is [He] \(2 s^2 2 p^1\). So, in first ionisation ( \(1 \mathrm{IE}_1\) or \(\Delta_i H_1\) ) removal will take place from unpaired \(p^1\)-electron. Whereas that of Be will be from paired \(2 s^2\)-electrons which requires more energy.
Electronic configuration of \(\mathrm{Be}(Z=4):[\mathrm{He}] 2 s^2\) So, the Assertion is a correct statement.
Reason (R) \(s\)-orbital is being symmetrical in shape (spherical), it shields nuclear force (nuclear charge) strongly. So, \(2 p^1\)-electron of \(B\) is experiences lesser nuclear attractive force for ionisation. As a result,

Nitrogen's higher ionisation enthalpy makes it less favourable to lose electrons compared to oxygen.
Oxygen's smaller atomic size allows for easier removal of electrons, resulting in a negative electron gain enthalpy.
questions.solution:
Correct Option is : (A)
Nitrogen's stable half-filled p-orbital (2p³) resists the addition of extra electrons, resulting in positive electron gain enthalpy.
